history.summary: Madurai's defining temple, dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar. Legend traces the shrine to Pandya king Kulasekera Pandya (6th century CE; some accounts claim a 6th century BC origin — verify, disputed). Glorified by the Nayanar saint Thirugnanasambandar (7th century), it was largely destroyed in the 1310 invasion of Malik Kafur and restored/rebuilt from the late 14th century, reaching its present 14-gopuram form under the Nayaks, especially Tirumalai Nayaka (16th-17th century). The complex spans ~14 acres, with the 170-ft southern gopuram the tallest, the Hall of Thousand Pillars (Ayiramkal Mandapam, 1569), the Golden Lotus Tank, and some 33,000 sculptures.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
town_description: Ancient temple city on the Vaigai river in southern Tamil Nadu, among the oldest continuously inhabited cities of India; also home to the Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace, Gandhi Museum and Koodal Azhagar Temple.

travel.road: Central Madurai, near the Vaigai river's south bank; well connected by city buses, autos and taxis

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Chithirai festival (April-May) is the biggest but most crowded
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM – 12:30 PM, 4:00 PM – 9:30 PM; mobile phones and cameras prohibited inside; Palliarai pooja 9:30-10:00 PM
